question: What are papers that train multilmodal language models that can input and output both text and images?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer lists the papers training multimodal models that can both understand and generate text and images: Chameleon, CM3, and Transfusion.
examples: The papers are Chameleon [0], CM3 [1], and Transfusion [2]
Relevant works include Chameleon, CM3, and Transfusion

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies Chameleon as a family of early-fusion, token-based mixed-modal foundation models capable of understanding and generating images and text in any arbitrary sequence.
examples: Chameleon is an early-fusion token-based mixed-modal model capable of understanding and generating images and text in any arbitrary sequence
Chameleon is a family of early-fusion token-based mixed-modal foundation models with a stable training approach and alignment recipe

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer describes Chameleon as representing images, text, and code as discrete tokens within a single uniform transformer-based architecture.
examples: It represents images, text, and code as discrete tokens and uses a uniform transformer-based architecture
Chameleon tokenizes both modalities into a shared discrete vocabulary processed by one transformer

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies CM3 as a family of causally masked generative models trained over a large corpus of structured multimodal documents containing both text and image tokens.
examples: CM3 is a family of causally masked generative models trained over a large corpus of structured multimodal documents with text and image tokens
CM3 is trained on multimodal internet documents that contain both text and image tokens

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains CM3's causal masking: left-to-right generation while a small number of long token spans are masked and generated at the end, forming a hybrid of causal and masked language models that gives bidirectional context for masked spans.
examples: CM3 generates tokens left to right but masks a few long spans generated at the end instead of their original positions
The causal masking objective combines causal and masked LM objectives, giving bidirectional context when generating masked spans

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies Transfusion as a recipe for training a single multimodal model over discrete and continuous data.
examples: Transfusion is a recipe for training multi-modal models over discrete and continuous data
Transfusion trains a single multimodal model on mixed discrete/continuous data

ingredients.name: answer_critical_5
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains that Transfusion combines the language modeling loss (next token prediction) with a diffusion objective to train a single transformer over mixed-modality sequences.
examples: Transfusion combines next-token prediction with diffusion losses in one transformer
It trains a single transformer over discrete and continuous data using LM loss plus diffusion

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer organizes the papers into two categories: fully autoregressive models that generate images as discrete tokens (Chameleon, CM3) versus autoregressive-text + diffusion-image models (Transfusion).
examples: Chameleon and CM3 generate images autoregressively as tokens, while Transfusion uses diffusion for images
Two paradigms exist: fully token-based AR generation and hybrid AR-text + diffusion-image models

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer may optionally cite additional unified autoregressive-text + diffusion-image models such as Show-O, which combines autoregressive and discrete diffusion modeling for mixed-modal inputs and outputs.
examples: Show-O combines autoregressive and discrete diffusion modeling for vision-language tasks like VQA and text-to-image generation
Other works connect diffusion image generation with autoregressive text models
